en: The Sūtra of the Two Dragon Kings’ Brothers, translated by the Wu-period Yuezhi Upāsaka Zhi Qian.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park in the kingdom of Śrāvastī.
At that time, there was an incalculable assembly of bhikṣus, all of whom were arhats.
Ānanda and Bimbisāra went to where the Buddha was, paid their respects, and withdrew to sit.
The Buddha said, "A person should practice giving, uphold the precepts, practice patience, exert diligence, cultivate meditative concentration, and develop wisdom.
Upon hearing this, Ānanda-Bhadrika was filled with joy; he immediately rose and addressed the Buddha:
"Tomorrow morning, I invite the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus to deign to visit my home; I shall provide them with simple food.
The Buddha remained silent.
Ānanda-Baṃdhi circumambulated the Buddha three times and departed.
The Buddha told the assembly of bhikṣus:
"Tomorrow morning we shall ascend to heaven, descend at noon, and gather at the house of Anāthapiṇḍada.
In the time it takes to extend one's arm, the Buddha remained suspended in mid-air.
The Arhat named Sudāna adjusted his robes and, kneeling upright in mid-air, addressed the Buddha:
"I have always ascended and descended, yet never before have I been as obscured as I am today."
The Buddha said, "There are two dragon kings who, out of anger, have manifested a transformation; it is because they have exhaled their breath to form clouds.
Furthermore, there was an arhat named Āyuṣmān who addressed the Buddha:
"I wish to stop its movement," [the king] said.
The Buddha replied,
"This dragon possesses great majestic power."
"You practitioner, you shall surely give rise to an evil intent and emerge from the water to submerge and kill the people of the world.
Mahāmaudgalyāyana again adjusted his robes, knelt upright in mid-air, and asked the Buddha:
"It is already dark today; I no longer see Mount Sumeru, the palace of Śakra, or the Nyagrodha tree below it."
The Buddha said,
"There were two dragon kings, one named Nanda and the other named Upananda, who became greatly incensed and said:
'What kind of śramaṇa wishes to fly over and rub his head upon my heads?'"
"The dragon’s body encircles Mount Sumeru seven times, covering its summit with its head; it emits mist from its breath, which is why it is so dark.
Maudgalyāyana addressed the Buddha, "I wish to go and rebuke and stop it."
The Buddha said,
"Excellent! Maudgalyāyana then circumambulated the Buddha three times and departed.
Śakra Devānām Indra was enjoying himself in the rear garden with eighty-eight thousand jade maidens.
Maudgalyāyana passed by their location first; the Lord of Devas came forward to meet him and prostrated himself in salutation.
Having exchanged greetings, he proceeded to the place where the two nāgas were.
Upon seeing him, the two nāgas became greatly incensed; they immediately manifested smoke through their supernatural power, and in a brief moment, they further emitted fire.
By the Buddha’s intent, Maudgalyāyana also manifested smoke that encircled the two dragons in three layers.

He then gradually moved forward, dividing his body to enter into the bodies of the two dragons; he entered through the right eye and emerged from the left, and entered through the left eye and emerged from the right.
Entering through the right ear, it exits through the left ear;
entering through the left ear, it exits through the right ear;
then it enters the right nostril and exits through the left nostril.
Entering through the left nostril and exiting through the right, it flew into his mouth.
The two dragons thought that Maudgalyāyana was within their bellies.
Maudgalyāyana likewise assumed the body of a dragon and coiled fourteen times around the two dragons, covering Mount Sumeru and the two dragons with his head.
The two dragons, trembling with fear below, caused Mount Sumeru to shake and sway; they lashed and fanned the ocean waters with their tails, and all the beasts were struck with terror.
From afar, the Buddha addressed Maudgalyāyana:
"These dragons shall now emerge from the water and submerge themselves to destroy the world."
"You must stop for a moment!
Maudgalyāyana said,
"I have heard this Dharma from the Buddha."
I possess the four bases of spiritual power; you should believe in, uphold, and practice them.
I am able to take these two nāgas and Mount Sumeru, place them in the palm of my hand, and leap across to another world-system;
I can also take Mount Sumeru, grind it down, and reduce it to dust.
"Furthermore, you can grind Mount Sumeru and the lands below so that the myriad people do not perceive it.
The two dragons were terrified; they prostrated themselves, and Maudgalyāyana restored them to their original forms as śramaṇas.
The two dragons transformed themselves into human form, prostrated before Maudgalyāyana, and repented their transgressions. Maudgalyāyana led them to the Buddha’s presence.
The two dragons said, “We were deluded and confused;
not knowing you were a venerable sage, we offended you with our thunderous roar. We pray that you compassionately pardon our offense!”
He then received the five precepts and departed.
Ānanda-Bhadrika went to the monastery and sought out the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus, but not a single person was to be seen.
He knelt down for a long time and said to the Buddha, "The meal preparations are fully arranged; may the Buddha deign to come."
The Buddha then descended to his house.
After the meal was finished, Anāthapiṇḍada said, "I sought the Buddha but did not see him; from where has the Buddha come?"
The Buddha said:
"Maudgalyāyana was just now descending from the heavens after having a dispute with the two dragon kings.
He asked:
"Who was victorious?
The Buddha replied,
"Maudgalyāyana."
Ānanda-Baṃdhi said:
"Excellent! Excellent!"

This dragon’s adherence to the precepts is firm and strong; yet for a transgression as slight as a hair’s breadth, his offense reaches the status of a dragon, and his majestic spiritual power is so venerable that even Maudgalyāyana must submit before him!
"From this day forward, I request that the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus proclaim the merits of Maudgalyāyana.
The Buddha then offered a blessing for the householder Anāthapiṇḍada:
"May you and those who have attained the Way through your offerings of food, both past and present, be protected by benevolent spirits; may your household be kept secure and peaceful."
Ānanda-bhadrika paid his respects and departed.
*The Sutra of the Dragon King Brothers*
